claims.title: Normalized zero-sum latent directions are exactly differences of disjoint-support latent probability mixtures
claims.scope: finite latent simplex with total-variation normalization TV(delta)=1
assumptions: delta sums to zero and is nonzero
nonclaims: the decomposition concerns signed tangent directions, not physical negative probabilities

claims.title: TV distance between two disjoint latent faces is an exact finite zero-sum event game
claims.scope: finite categorical channel and two disjoint nonempty latent row subsets
assumptions: the exact rational game support search completes below its configured cap
nonclaims: the bounded exact solver is not asserted polynomial time

claims.title: Minimum disjoint-face separation equals the global latent-to-observed TV modulus alpha(K)
assumptions: all disjoint nonempty face pairs and observed events are enumerated below explicit caps
nonclaims: alpha is a conditioning modulus rather than a posterior probability

claims.title: The exact inverse TV constant is 1/alpha and cannot exceed any valid coordinate-minor inverse certificate
nonclaims: a conservative coordinate certificate is not an identifiability failure

claims.title: Uniformly positive pairwise component separation does not lower-bound finite-mixture conditioning away from zero
claims.scope: the three-row epsilon family K0=(1,0,0), K1=(0,1,0), K2=(1/2,1/2-epsilon,epsilon) for rational 0<epsilon<1/2
assumptions: TV is used on the observed simplex
nonclaims: the result does not say pairwise separation is useless for component classification

claims.title: Identity K3 has alpha one and exact inverse constant one while the generic coordinate-minor certificate returns two
claims.scope: identity channel on three latent and three observed symbols
nonclaims: the factor-two coordinate gap is specific to that generic certificate

claims.title: The near-midpoint three-row family has pairwise TV separation one-half but global alpha equal to epsilon
claims.scope: rational epsilon values tested at 1/4, 1/5, 1/8, and 1/10
assumptions: the declared channel rows are exact
nonclaims: the finite test grid is not the proof of the symbolic family theorem

claims.title: Bounded exact global finite-mixture TV-modulus audit
claims.scope: identity, binary noisy, exact midpoint, near-midpoint epsilon family, event caps, face caps, and exact primal-dual game receipts
assumptions: all configured event, face, minor, and game-support searches complete
all channel probabilities are exact rationals
nonclaims: bounded enumeration is not a scalability theorem
CI success is not evidence for simulation
